To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a customized annotation schema and a well defined use case for information extraction can help to focus the annotation task and improve agreement among human annotators; (2) the annotation schema should be designed to be as specific and detailed as possible; (3) the highest concept yield is achieved when focusing annotation on specific note types and document sections; and (4) the highest concept agreement is achieved when focusing on the document and concept levels of annotation.

(1) we developed a manually annotated corpus to identify phenotypical information in the clinical notes for patients with IBD, and (2) we identified specific challenges and opportunities for annotation tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the annotation of clinical documents for the purpose of extracting phenotypic information from the clinical note.
identifying and addressing challenges and opportunities in creating clinical document corpora that are manually annotated to support specific use cases.
developing and testing methods to create a reference standard for NLP IE systems to identify phenotypically relevant information from clinical notes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a method for creating a reference standard for a specific use case and have demonstrated the utility of this approach in a clinical document corpus for patients with IBD.

the development of a manually annotated clinical note corpus for a specific use case can be accomplished with the appropriate resources, but that the process requires careful consideration of the specific challenges and opportunities.
the annotation process for clinical notes is complex, but the results are useful and can help to focus and clarify the NLP system requirements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the annotation process is time consuming and requires a great deal of effort, but the resulting annotated corpus is useful for training and validating NLP systems and for identifying specific NLP system requirements.
the development of a clinical document corpus and the creation of an annotated reference standard is a challenging, but worthwhile task.
the development of an annotated corpus for phenotypic data extraction is an iterative process that requires a significant time investment and a clear focus for information extraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the process of annotating clinical documents for specific information extraction tasks requires considerable effort and time.
it is possible to build a clinical corpus with high annotator agreement and reasonable concept yield.
a clinician annotated corpus is an essential resource for NLP IE system development.
